en: Points of Controversy:
The Chapter on Latent Dispositions,
Fourteenth Section.
The Discussion on the Linking of the Wholesome and the Unwholesome:
Does an unwholesome root link up with a wholesome root?
Yes, it does.
Is that which is a turning toward, ... down to ... an aspiration for the arising of the unwholesome, the same as the turning toward, ... down to ... the aspiration for the arising of the wholesome?
One should not say so ... [as before] ...
The root of the unwholesome connects with the root of the wholesome; one should not say this.
“Is that which is a turning toward, … down to … a longing for the arising of the unwholesome, the very same as the turning toward, … down to … the longing for the arising of the wholesome?”— Yes.
[Then] does it arise for one who is not turning toward the wholesome, … down to … for one who is not longing for it?— Yes.
It should not be stated thus … [as before] … Is it not the case that wholesome [consciousness] arises for one who is turning back toward [the object], … [as before] … and for one who is aspiring?
Yes, it is.
If [an unwholesome root] arises for one who is turning toward the wholesome …pe… for one who is aspiring toward it, then surely you should not say:
"An unwholesome root connects with a wholesome root.
Is it the case that an unwholesome root connects with a wholesome root?
“Yes.
“Does it arise for one who attends to things in an improper manner?
“Yes.”
“Does the wholesome arise for one who attends to it inappropriately?
“One should not say so.
…pe… “Does the wholesome not rather arise for one who attends to it appropriately?”
“Yes.
“If it is indeed the case that the wholesome arises for one who attends wisely, then surely you should not say:
‘An unwholesome root connects with a wholesome root.’”
Is an unwholesome root connected with a wholesome root? Yes.
Immediately after a perception of sensual desire, a perception of renunciation arises; immediately after a perception of ill will, a perception of non-ill will arises.
Does non-harming perception arise immediately after the perception of harming; does loving-kindness arise immediately after ill-will;
does compassion arise immediately after cruelty; does sympathetic joy arise immediately after discontent;
and does equanimity arise immediately after aversion?
It should not be said thus… [as before]… Does a wholesome root link up with an unwholesome root? Yes.

Is that which is the turning toward, the inclination, and the aspiration for the arising of the wholesome, the very same as the turning toward, the inclination, and the aspiration for the arising of the unwholesome?
One should not say so... [etc.
...The root of the wholesome reconnects with the root of the unwholesome; one should not say so.
“If that which is an inclination … down to … a wish for the arising of the wholesome is itself an inclination … down to … a wish for the arising of the unwholesome,” you say, “Yes.
Then does it arise for one who does not incline toward the unwholesome … down to … does it arise for one who does not wish for it? [You must answer,] “Yes.”

It should not be said so … [as before] … Is it not the case that unwholesome states arise for one who is turning back [from them], and so on, up to: do they arise for one who is aspiring [toward them]?
Yes, they do.
If unwholesome [kamma] arises for one who is turning back toward it …pe… for one who is aspiring toward it, then surely you should not say:
"A wholesome root is linked with an unwholesome root.
Is it the case that a wholesome root is linked with an unwholesome root?
“Yes.
“Does it arise for one who attends wisely?
“Yes.”
“Does unwholesome [kamma] arise for one who attends to it improperly?
One should not say so … pe … “Is it not the case that unwholesome [kamma] arises for one who attends to it improperly?”
“Yes.
“If unwholesome states arise for one who attends to things in an improper way,
then surely it should not be said that ‘a wholesome root connects with an unwholesome root.’”
Is a wholesome root connected with an unwholesome root? Yes.
Immediately after the perception of renunciation, the perception of sensual desire arises; immediately after the perception of non-ill will, the perception of ill will arises.
Does non-harming-perception arise, and immediately after non-harming-perception does harming-perception arise; does ill-will arise immediately after loving-kindness,
violence arise immediately after compassion, discontent arise immediately after sympathetic joy,
and aversion arise immediately after equanimity?
It should not be said thus... [as before] ...
Should it not be said:
"An unwholesome root links up with a wholesome root; a wholesome root links up with an unwholesome root"?
“Yes,” he says.
“Is it not the case that one feels passion for the very same object for which one feels dispassion, and that one feels dispassion for the very same object for which one feels passion?
“Yes,” he says.
If one is attached to the very same object that one becomes detached from, and if one becomes detached from the very same object that one is attached to, then indeed it must be said:
"An unwholesome root connects with a wholesome root; a wholesome root connects with an unwholesome root. The discussion on the connection between wholesome and unwholesome roots is concluded.
